decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Molecular and Cell Biology
decks.description: Integrate modern molecular and cellular evidence.

includes: Chromatin, RNA regulation, proteostasis, single-cell assays and causal perturbation design

practice: Design a single-cell perturbation study and analyze supplied multi-assay data to distinguish regulatory mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Construct perturbation, rescue and temporal experiments that separate direct effects, compensation and correlated cellular states.
Analyze chromatin, RNA regulation, proteostasis and organelle dynamics using competing molecular mechanisms and perturbation evidence.
Design and analyze single-cell expression, accessibility and imaging workflows with lineage, batch, dropout and state-versus-fate distinctions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Physiology
decks.description: Predict integrated animal physiological responses.

includes: Comparative transport, gas exchange, renal, endocrine, digestive, muscular and reproductive physiology
excludes: Clinical practice and detailed neural computation

practice: Analyze a comparative exercise or environmental-stress dataset using mass balance, feedback and transport calculations.

outcomes.description: Predict integrated responses to exercise, fasting and environmental stress and design physiological measurements separating mechanisms.
Explain endocrine feedback, osmoregulation, thermoregulation, muscle contraction and reproductive control using comparative anatomy.
Apply explicitly taught pressure-flow, diffusion and clearance models to circulation, respiration, digestion and excretion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biochemistry
decks.description: Connect molecular structure with biochemical function.

includes: Biomolecular structure, binding, enzyme kinetics and biochemical free-energy accounting
excludes: Full metabolic networks and structural reconstruction

practice: Compare binding and inhibition models for an enzyme dataset and design an assay separating catalytic from stability effects.

outcomes.description: Calculate equilibrium binding and cooperativity using taught occupancy models; distinguish affinity, specificity and avidity.
Relate protein, nucleic-acid, carbohydrate and lipid structures to folding, recognition and chemical function.
Calculate biochemical free-energy changes, coupled reactions and redox driving forces using stated standard states and assumptions.
Derive the bounded steady-state Michaelis-Menten model algebraically and interpret inhibition and enzyme-assay data.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Bioinformatics and Genomics
decks.description: Infer biological information from sequence-scale data.

includes: Sequence algorithms, read analysis, genomic variation, expression and reproducible biological inference

practice: Implement an alignment kernel and analyze a small unfamiliar sequencing dataset with a reproducible uncertainty and provenance report.

outcomes.description: Run documented read-quality, mapping, assembly, variant and expression workflows with reference, coverage and batch diagnostics.
Assess annotation, enrichment and phylogenetic evidence using null models, multiplicity correction and reproducible provenance.
Implement pairwise sequence alignment with dynamic programming and explain scoring, indexing and heuristic-search tradeoffs.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biostatistics and Study Design
decks.description: Design and analyze robust biological studies.

includes: Biological design, multivariable models, generalized and hierarchical models using documented software

practice: Preregister and analyze a blocked biological study, comparing model diagnostics and sensitivity to missingness and batch adjustment.

outcomes.description: Design factorial, blocked, repeated-measures and observational studies with power, confounding and pseudoreplication checks.
Specify linear, logistic, count and mixed models with design matrices and likelihood notation; fit and diagnose them using software.
Handle multiplicity, missingness and batch effects; produce reproducible analyses distinguishing exploratory from confirmatory claims.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology
decks.description: Explain cellular organization and perturbation responses.

includes: Membranes, organelles, cytoskeleton, transport, signaling and cell-cycle control
excludes: Detailed omics and molecular experimental machinery

practice: Analyze a cellular perturbation dataset and design complementary localization and transport tests for competing mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Explain organelle function, protein sorting, vesicle traffic, cytoskeletal organization and cell-matrix interactions.
Trace receptor signaling, feedback, division and cell death and propose observations distinguishing pathway defects.
Predict diffusion, osmosis and carrier-mediated transport using concentration gradients and explicitly taught electrochemical-potential models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology
decks.description: Use ecological evidence to justify interventions.

includes: Biodiversity assessment, demographic risk, connectivity, restoration and conservation decisions

practice: Prepare a conservation decision dossier with population projections, monitoring triggers and explicit stakeholder tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Estimate biodiversity and extinction risk using detection-aware surveys and locally developed stage-structured population matrices.
Defend an adaptive-management decision considering uncertainty, Indigenous and local knowledge, distributional impacts and competing objectives.
Compare reserve, connectivity, harvest, invasive-species and restoration strategies using demographic and genetic evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Infer mechanisms that build biological form.

includes: Gene regulation, patterning, lineage, morphogenesis and comparative development

practice: Infer a developmental mechanism from lineage and perturbation data and propose a decisive rescue experiment.

outcomes.description: Design lineage-tracing, transplantation and perturbation experiments and distinguish specification, determination and environmental effects.
Relate lineage, cell mechanics, migration and programmed death to tissue morphogenesis and regeneration.
Explain positional information, induction, gene-regulatory patterning and cell-fate stabilization in animal and plant examples.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Disease Biology and Biotechnology
decks.description: Evaluate biological interventions from mechanism to population.

includes: Disease mechanisms, epidemiological inference, biotechnology, therapeutic development and translational judgment
excludes: Clinical diagnosis, treatment and practitioner authorization

practice: Prepare an intervention dossier integrating mechanistic experiments, a population study and explicit benefit-risk and access judgments.

outcomes.description: Explain infectious, genetic, metabolic and neoplastic disease mechanisms and evaluate model-organism and organoid evidence.
Design cohort, case-control and trial analyses; calculate risk measures and use explicitly taught discrete transmission models with bias checks.
Design bounded diagnostic, therapeutic or engineered-biological workflows and justify efficacy, safety, access, dual-use and consent decisions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology
decks.description: Explain organism-environment systems with field evidence.

includes: Population recurrences, communities, ecosystems and ecological field inference

practice: Conduct or reconstruct a field survey and compare population and community explanations with explicit detection assumptions.

outcomes.description: Analyze competition, predation, mutualism, food webs, productivity and nutrient budgets across ecological scales.
Design quadrat, transect and mark-recapture studies; estimate abundance and distinguish detection bias from ecological change.
Construct discrete growth, survival and resource-use models and interpret density dependence and life-history data.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology
decks.description: Explain and test evolutionary change.

includes: Selection, drift, migration, phylogenetic reasoning, adaptation and speciation

practice: Analyze an unfamiliar evolutionary pattern with allele-frequency predictions and competing phylogenetic explanations.

outcomes.description: Evaluate adaptation, life-history, speciation and extinction explanations using comparative, fossil and experimental evidence.
Calculate Hardy-Weinberg and elementary selection or migration recurrences and distinguish drift from deterministic predictions.
Construct small character-based phylogenies and compare homology, convergence and elementary likelihood-based tree evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Experimental Methods
decks.description: Collect reproducible biological observations.

includes: Microscopy, specimen handling, biological controls, records and research ethics

practice: Conduct a blinded microscopy comparison with calibrated images, independent replicates, an artifact audit and an ethical justification.

outcomes.description: Justify specimen, consent, welfare, data-integrity and environmental decisions by comparing harms, scientific value and alternatives.
Plan controls, replication and randomization; perform dilution and basic sampling procedures and document complete protocols.
Prepare specimens, calibrate light-microscope scale and resolution, and quantify images with sampling and artifact checks.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Foundations
decks.description: Explain biological organization using testable mechanisms.

includes: Cells, organisms, heredity, energy, evolution and biological evidence

practice: Explain an unfamiliar organismal adaptation with a causal diagram and propose observations that could disconfirm the explanation.

outcomes.description: Distinguish observations, hypotheses and causal claims; interpret simple biological graphs and propose controlled comparisons.
Represent cellular components and levels of organization and distinguish major cellular and organismal forms.
Explain information inheritance, matter and energy flow, reproduction and natural selection using bounded examples.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics
decks.description: Infer genetic transmission from observed variation.

includes: Mendelian inheritance, linkage, mutation, pedigrees and elementary quantitative traits

practice: Infer a genetic model and linkage map from unfamiliar crosses, documenting uncertainty and inconsistent observations.

outcomes.description: Predict crosses and pedigrees involving dominance, sex linkage, penetrance, epistasis and non-Mendelian inheritance.
Infer linkage, recombination distances and gene order from cross data and test alternative inheritance models.
Explain mutation and chromosomal variation; partition simple trait variation and interpret heritability without genetic determinism.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immune protection and dysfunction.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity, antigen recognition, tolerance, memory and immune assays

practice: Interpret an unfamiliar immune-response dataset and design an assay separating recognition failure from effector dysfunction.

outcomes.description: Design and interpret ELISA, flow-cytometry and functional immune assays with gating, specificity and control strategies.
Explain innate sensing, antigen processing, receptor diversification and lymphocyte selection with molecular and cellular representations.
Predict effector, memory and tolerance responses and distinguish infection control, autoimmunity, allergy and immune evasion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Metabolism and Bioenergetics
decks.description: Account for biological matter, electrons and energy.

includes: Central metabolism, electron transport, photosynthesis and tissue-level metabolic integration

practice: Reconcile isotope-label and metabolite data with competing pathway explanations and predict a held-out perturbation.

outcomes.description: Calculate ATP and redox balances in respiration and photosynthesis; explain chemiosmosis and coupling limitations.
Predict pathway regulation and metabolic adaptation to fasting, exercise, nutrient limitation or enzyme perturbation.
Trace carbon, nitrogen and reducing equivalents through carbohydrate, lipid, amino-acid and nucleotide pathways.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology
decks.description: Characterize microbes and their biological interactions.

includes: Microbial physiology, culture, identification, resistance, ecology and viral life cycles

practice: Characterize an approved isolate using growth, microscopy and identification evidence, or analyze an equivalent archived dataset.

outcomes.description: Compare bacterial, archaeal and microbial-eukaryotic structure, metabolism, ecological roles and gene-transfer mechanisms.
Measure growth and viable counts and explain environmental tolerance, antimicrobial action and resistance selection.
Use aseptic culture, staining and biochemical or sequence evidence to identify approved organisms with contamination controls.
Represent viral entry, genome replication, assembly and transmission and interpret plaque and host-range evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Biology
decks.description: Explain and experimentally interrogate genetic information flow.

includes: Replication, expression, regulation, nucleic-acid assays and genetic manipulation

practice: Design and interpret a safe reporter or supplied gene-editing experiment that distinguishes expression from protein-function defects.

outcomes.description: Explain replication, repair, recombination, transcription, RNA processing and translation with sequence and molecular representations.
Design PCR, electrophoresis, cloning, sequencing and bounded genome-editing workflows with controls and specificity checks.
Infer transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation from reporter, expression and perturbation evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience and Behavior
decks.description: Connect neural mechanisms with computation and behavior.

includes: Neural excitability, synapses, sensory and motor circuits, plasticity and behavior

practice: Analyze stimulus-response and behavioral data and propose circuit interventions distinguishing competing coding hypotheses.

outcomes.description: Design electrophysiological and behavioral comparisons that distinguish neural mechanism, learning, motivation and measurement confounds.
Trace sensory, motor and autonomic pathways and interpret coding, synaptic plasticity and circuit perturbations.
Calculate resting and synaptic potentials using taught Nernst and equivalent-circuit models; explain action-potential generation.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Organismal Diversity
decks.description: Compare organisms through structure and life history.

includes: Major lineages, comparative anatomy, reproduction and life-cycle representations

practice: Build an evidence-based identification key and comparative anatomical and life-cycle atlas for unfamiliar specimens.

outcomes.description: Compare body plans, tissues and organ arrangements and relate structural differences to functional constraints.
Use diagnostic characters and branching diagrams to distinguish major microbial, fungal, plant and animal lineages.
Construct sexual, asexual and alternation-of-generation life cycles, tracking ploidy and transmission stages.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology
decks.description: Explain plant function through structure and regulation.

includes: Plant anatomy, water and mineral transport, photosynthesis, growth and environmental responses

practice: Measure or analyze plant responses to water and light treatments, separating anatomical, stomatal and biochemical explanations.

outcomes.description: Calculate water-potential and gas-exchange responses; explain mineral uptake, phloem transport and photosynthetic alternatives.
Predict hormonal, photoperiodic and stress responses and design controlled growth or transport experiments.
Identify plant tissues, meristems and reproductive structures and relate development to vascular organization.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population Genetics and Genomics
decks.description: Infer evolutionary processes from genetic variation.

includes: Selection-drift models, linkage, coalescent genealogies and evolutionary genomic inference

practice: Analyze an unfamiliar population-genomic dataset and test whether inferred selection survives alternative demographic and sampling models.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary coalescent waiting-time models and relate genealogies, recombination and demographic history to sequence summaries.
Fit and compare demographic, ancestry and selection models using documented likelihood or simulation workflows and confounding diagnostics.
Construct finite Wright-Fisher and selection-migration models and calculate drift, fixation and linkage-disequilibrium behavior.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology and Biophysics
decks.description: Infer biomolecular structure from physical evidence.

includes: Structural diffraction, NMR restraints, cryo-EM reconstruction, biophysical validation and model uncertainty

practice: Reconstruct a bounded synthetic density and evaluate a real structural model against diffraction, restraint or projection evidence.

outcomes.description: Derive reciprocal-space diffraction and Fourier-density relations; explain phase recovery and refine bounded structural models against intensities.
Implement small projection-reconstruction and alignment exercises; validate cryo-EM maps and molecular models using resolution and independent evidence.
Interpret multidimensional NMR correlations and distance restraints using locally taught spin and assignment models; assess ensemble ambiguity.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology and Neural Modeling
decks.description: Construct and test mechanistic biological dynamical models.

includes: Reaction networks, metabolic constraints, dynamical inference and conductance-based neural models

practice: Implement a cellular or neural model, fit time-course data and design a perturbation resolving a parameter ambiguity.

outcomes.description: Fit dynamical parameters and analyze sensitivity, structural nonidentifiability, bootstrap uncertainty and held-out perturbation predictions.
Construct stoichiometric and regulatory networks, derive mass-action ODEs and solve bounded flux-balance and stability problems.
Derive and implement membrane conductance, gating and integrate-and-fire models and analyze excitability and small neural networks.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Theoretical Ecology
decks.description: Analyze ecological dynamics and hidden processes.

includes: Population interactions, stage structure, metapopulations, stochasticity and model-based inference

practice: Implement and fit an interacting-population model, testing stability predictions against held-out perturbation and detection data.

outcomes.description: Derive and analyze consumer-resource, competition and stage-structured models using equilibria, eigenvalues and bifurcation diagrams.
Fit ecological state and observation models using documented likelihood procedures; assess identifiability and out-of-sample predictions.
Implement finite-patch dispersal and stochastic population models and quantify persistence, invasion and environmental variability.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Explain inorganic bonding and catalytic mechanisms quantitatively.

includes: Molecular symmetry, ligand-field and orbital bonding, organometallic mechanisms and catalysis

practice: Infer a catalytic cycle from spectroscopic and rate evidence and propose an experiment distinguishing turnover-limiting alternatives.

outcomes.description: Derive molecular-orbital and ligand-field descriptions and interpret electronic, magnetic and structural evidence in complexes.
Analyze substitution, electron transfer and organometallic catalytic cycles using electron counting, energetics, kinetics and mechanistic controls.
Construct molecular point-group operations and use locally developed character and projection methods for orbital and vibrational symmetry.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry
decks.description: Develop mechanistic and strategic graduate organic reasoning.

includes: Physical-organic inference, orbital symmetry, stereocontrol and advanced synthetic strategy

practice: Defend competing routes to an unfamiliar stereochemical target using mechanistic experiments and orbital arguments.

outcomes.description: Apply frontier-orbital and orbital-symmetry arguments to pericyclic, photochemical and stereoselective reactions.
Infer transition-state and mechanistic structure using substituent effects, isotope effects, kinetic data and stereochemical probes.
Design convergent and asymmetric synthetic strategies and compare catalyst, selectivity, robustness and material-efficiency tradeoffs.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry
decks.description: Determine chemical quantities with validated evidence.

includes: Coupled solution equilibria, titrimetry, gravimetry, calibration and analytical validation

practice: Quantify an unknown mixture with two methods and explain discrepancies through equilibrium, calibration and matrix-effect evidence.

outcomes.description: Solve coupled acid-base, complexation, precipitation and redox balances, checking approximations and numerical root-solver residuals.
Determine concentrations by titration, gravimetry and Beer-Lambert calibration, including blanks, standard additions and recovery.
Estimate analytical uncertainty, detection limits and bias; design validation and select methods for sample-matrix constraints.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Statistical Chemical Dynamics
decks.description: Connect molecular motion with rates and relaxation.

includes: Molecular partition functions, reaction-rate theory, diffusion, master equations and relaxation

practice: Predict a molecular rate and relaxation curve from an energy landscape and discriminate diffusion- from activation-limited behavior.

outcomes.description: Construct molecular partition functions and calculate thermodynamic and equilibrium properties from translational, rotational and vibrational states.
Derive transition-state and elementary collision-theory rates and assess recrossing, tunneling and solvent-friction limitations.
Solve reaction-diffusion and finite-state master-equation models and relate correlation functions to relaxation and time-resolved spectra.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
decks.description: Predict equilibrium in reacting and multiphase mixtures.

includes: Chemical potential, partial molar properties, activities, phase diagrams and reaction equilibria

practice: Construct a binary phase diagram and equilibrium composition model and test sensitivity to nonideality and standard-state choices.

outcomes.description: Derive chemical potentials, partial molar properties and Gibbs-Duhem constraints from thermodynamic differentials.
Predict reaction equilibria and binary phase diagrams with consistent standard states, stability and temperature dependence.
Calculate ideal and bounded nonideal mixture behavior using activities, fugacities and phase-equilibrium conditions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Chemistry
decks.description: Validate molecular calculations across model scales.

includes: Electronic workflows, molecular simulation, force fields, sampling and free-energy estimation

practice: Compare electronic and force-field predictions for a molecular transformation, reporting convergence and sampling uncertainty separately.

outcomes.description: Run and validate electronic-structure optimizations, frequencies and reaction paths with basis, correlation and convergence diagnostics.
Estimate free-energy differences with taught reweighting and thermodynamic-integration procedures, checking overlap, equilibration and uncertainty.
Implement a small force-field molecular-dynamics engine with periodic boundaries, integration and energy-drift tests; compare thermostatted software runs.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Electrochemistry
decks.description: Analyze electrochemical conversion and measurement.

includes: Electrode thermodynamics, kinetic polarization, bounded transport models and electrochemical measurements

practice: Analyze a cell's polarization and impedance data and design controls distinguishing kinetic, resistive and mass-transfer losses.

outcomes.description: Calculate Nernst potentials, cell energetics, concentration effects and reference-electrode conversions with consistent conventions.
Apply taught Butler-Volmer, Tafel and diffusion-layer models, stating assumptions and separating charge-transfer and transport effects.
Interpret voltammetry and impedance with explicit equivalent-circuit models; compare corrosion, battery and sensor performance.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry
decks.description: Trace chemicals through environmental compartments.

includes: Atmospheric, aquatic and soil chemistry, contaminant fate, monitoring and remediation decisions

practice: Build a contaminant budget from environmental measurements and defend a monitoring and remediation strategy.

outcomes.description: Compare remediation and prevention options using chemical evidence, exposure pathways, uncertainty and unequal environmental burdens.
Calculate speciation, partitioning, residence times and first-order compartment fate; explain atmospheric photochemistry and redox transformations.
Design sampling, preservation, blanks and analytical workflows for air, water and soil contaminants.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Foundations
decks.description: Represent matter and predict simple transformations.

includes: Atomic models, chemical representations, bonding, stoichiometry, solution chemistry and simple equilibria
excludes: Quantum derivations and advanced reaction mechanisms

practice: Plan a solution reaction, predict composition and pH, and reconcile a supplied mass and heat dataset.

outcomes.description: Explain periodic trends and construct Lewis, resonance and molecular-geometry models with explicit limitations.
Calculate simple equilibrium and acid-base concentrations using mass action, charge balance, pH and justified approximations.
Translate formulas, particle models and macroscopic amounts; calculate composition, moles, concentrations and gas quantities.
Balance reactions and redox processes; calculate limiting reagents, yields, solution preparation and calorimetric changes.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Industrial and Process Chemistry
decks.description: Evaluate chemical processes through balances and risk.

includes: Reaction engineering, phase-based separations, flowsheets and process sustainability
excludes: Plant operating authorization and detailed equipment engineering

practice: Compare reactor-separation flowsheets for an unfamiliar reaction and document heat-removal, waste and upset-condition tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Compare flowsheets using yield, energy, waste, lifecycle boundaries and process-hazard scenarios; justify safer design choices.
Derive batch, stirred-tank and plug-flow material and energy balances; calculate conversion, residence time and thermal stability.
Calculate elementary distillation, extraction and recycle balances using phase-equilibrium and stage representations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry Foundations
decks.description: Interpret inorganic structures and chemical trends.

includes: Main-group chemistry, coordination compounds, crystal-field models and elementary solids

practice: Identify candidate formulas and structures from composition, magnetic and lattice data using explicit model limitations.

outcomes.description: Assign coordination geometry, isomerism, d-electron count and elementary crystal-field splitting, color and magnetism.
Use periodicity, oxidation states and acid-base or redox patterns to predict main-group structures and reactions.
Represent unit cells and common ionic structures; calculate occupancy, stoichiometry and simple defect charge balance.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Instrumental Analysis
decks.description: Develop validated instrumental chemical assays.

includes: Chromatographic separations, mass and optical instrumentation, multidimensional spectroscopy and chemometrics

practice: Develop an assay for a complex mixture and validate separation, structural identification, calibration and uncertainty with independent samples.

outcomes.description: Build multivariate calibration and spectral-decomposition models with documented software; validate detection, identification and transfer under matrix effects.
Explain source, analyzer and detector operation in optical and mass instruments and interpret tandem-MS and two-dimensional NMR evidence.
Design chromatographic and electrophoretic separations using retention, plate-height, selectivity and resolution models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics
decks.description: Infer chemical mechanisms from reaction rates.

includes: Rate laws, integrated kinetics, mechanisms, catalysis and temperature dependence

practice: Fit competing kinetic mechanisms to time-course data using documented fitting software and design a discriminating experiment.

outcomes.description: Derive rate expressions from elementary steps using pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations; discriminate nonunique mechanisms.
Derive and fit elementary integrated rate laws and compare direct nonlinear fits with transformed plots.
Estimate Arrhenius parameters and analyze catalysis, competing pathways and experimental confounding in temperature-dependent rates.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Methods
decks.description: Execute reproducible introductory chemical investigations.

includes: Preparation, separation, elementary characterization, notebooks and chemical risk assessment

practice: Prepare and separate a safe mixture, documenting mass balance, purity evidence, uncertainty and a procedure-specific risk assessment.

outcomes.description: Perform weighing, volumetric preparation, heating, filtration, extraction, recrystallization and elementary chromatography with recovery calculations.
Maintain traceable notebooks; calibrate balances and volumetric tools and report replicate variability and yield uncertainty.
Compare procedure hazards, exposure controls, incompatibilities and waste routes; justify a safer feasible experimental design.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials Chemistry
decks.description: Synthesize and identify functional inorganic materials.

includes: Crystallography, defects, phase selection, solid-state synthesis and materials characterization

practice: Plan an approved material synthesis and infer phase composition from diffraction, thermal and elemental measurements.

outcomes.description: Index bounded powder-diffraction patterns and combine thermal, microscopic and compositional evidence to identify phases and defects.
Construct lattice and reciprocal-lattice representations, Miller indices and defect equilibria for common crystalline materials.
Plan ceramic, solution and thin-film synthesis using nucleation, phase stability, diffusion-scale estimates and composition control.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure and Reactivity
decks.description: Reason about organic structure and electron flow.

includes: Organic representations, stereochemistry, acid-base behavior and elementary reaction mechanisms

practice: Predict products and stereochemistry for an unfamiliar reaction set and explain plausible competing pathways.

outcomes.description: Draw valid electron-pushing mechanisms for acid-base, substitution, elimination, addition and elementary carbonyl reactions.
Predict relative reactivity using resonance, induction, sterics, aromaticity and qualitative kinetic versus thermodynamic control.
Translate skeletal, wedge-dash, Newman and chair representations; assign stereoisomers, conformation and functional groups.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis
decks.description: Plan and verify multistep organic transformations.

includes: Carbonyl and aromatic chemistry, selective transformations, retrosynthesis and experimental verification

practice: Develop competing routes to a small target and execute an approved step with complete characterization and mass balance.

outcomes.description: Construct multistep retrosyntheses using functional-group interconversion, protecting groups and carbon-carbon bond disconnections.
Predict chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity in carbonyl, aromatic, organometallic, oxidation and reduction transformations.
Plan reaction setup, workup and purification and verify product identity, purity, yield and alternative pathway evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry
decks.description: Connect macromolecular synthesis with material properties.

includes: Polymerization mechanisms, molecular-weight distributions, solution behavior and thermal properties

practice: Select a polymerization route for specified properties and reconcile molecular-weight and thermal-characterization data.

outcomes.description: Calculate number- and weight-average molecular masses, dispersity and simple chain statistics from distributions.
Design step-growth, chain-growth and copolymerization routes and predict architecture, conversion and termination effects.
Interpret polymer mixing, glass transition, crystallinity and viscoelastic measurements using explicitly taught bounded models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Predict molecular electronic structure and spectral behavior.

includes: Molecular Hamiltonians, orbital approximations, variational methods and molecular spectra

practice: Calculate a small molecule's approximate energy and spectrum and separate basis, correlation and experimental uncertainties.

outcomes.description: Derive variational and Hartree-Fock matrix procedures; iterate small supplied-integral models and compare correlation and density-functional approximations.
Construct Born-Oppenheimer molecular Hamiltonians and explain orbital, spin, antisymmetry and bonding representations.
Calculate rotational, vibrational and electronic transitions and selection rules for bounded molecular models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Spectroscopy and Structure
decks.description: Infer small-molecule structure from complementary spectra.

includes: Accessible IR, mass spectrometry and one-dimensional proton and carbon NMR interpretation
excludes: Quantum spectral derivations and macromolecular reconstruction

practice: Identify an unknown from incomplete spectra, rank alternatives and justify a decisive follow-up measurement.

outcomes.description: Combine orthogonal evidence to distinguish isomers, recognize mixtures and identify additional measurements resolving ambiguity.
Assign molecular formulas, functional groups, chemical shifts, integrations and simple coupling patterns to candidate structures.
Explain signal formation, axes, resolution and limitations of IR, mass and one-dimensional NMR using bounded physical models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Algorithms and Complexity
decks.description: Establish graduate algorithmic guarantees and limitations.

includes: Randomized analysis, approximation, online methods and advanced reductions

practice: Design an approximation or streaming algorithm, prove its guarantee and compare adversarial and typical empirical behavior.

outcomes.description: Design approximation and online algorithms using charging, primal-dual and locally developed linear-relaxation arguments.
Prove advanced time-space and approximation reductions and distinguish worst-case, parameterized and average-case claims.
Derive elementary concentration bounds and analyze randomized sampling, hashing and streaming algorithms with failure probabilities.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Machine Learning
decks.description: Connect learning algorithms with statistical guarantees.

includes: Generalization theory, advanced neural optimization, probabilistic models and sequential learning

practice: Derive a learning guarantee and test its assumptions in a reproducible latent-variable or sequential-learning study.

outcomes.description: Implement automatic-differentiation graphs and advanced neural models; analyze optimization, regularization and calibration failures.
Derive finite-class and capacity-based generalization bounds using locally proved concentration and symmetrization arguments.
Derive and implement bounded latent-variable, variational and policy-gradient methods and evaluate uncertainty and distribution shift.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Algorithms
decks.description: Design efficient algorithms with correctness arguments.

includes: Design paradigms, graph algorithms, correctness, recurrences and reductions

practice: Solve an unfamiliar scheduling or routing problem with competing algorithms, proofs, benchmarks and a reduction analysis.

outcomes.description: Solve cost recurrences, compare time-space tradeoffs and construct elementary hardness reductions.
Design divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic-programming algorithms with explicit subproblems and correctness invariants.
Implement traversal, shortest-path, spanning-tree and flow algorithms and prove their essential invariants.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Architecture
decks.description: Explain how hardware executes programs.

includes: Instruction sets, assembly, datapaths, caches, pipelines and performance models

practice: Build an emulator and benchmark programs that separate arithmetic, cache and branch bottlenecks.

outcomes.description: Write assembly and implement a small instruction-set emulator with registers, addressing, stack frames and exceptions.
Analyze caches, locality, memory hierarchy and basic virtual-address translation using address traces.
Analyze pipelining, hazards and parallel speedup and reconcile instruction-level models with benchmarks.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence
decks.description: Construct agents that search, infer and plan.

includes: Search, constraint satisfaction, knowledge representation, probabilistic inference and finite decision processes

practice: Build an agent for a partially uncertain task and compare planning quality, computational cost and reward-design failure modes.

outcomes.description: Formulate finite Markov decision processes and implement value iteration and tabular reinforcement learning with reward-risk analysis.
Represent rules and Bayesian networks and implement bounded logical and probabilistic inference.
Implement heuristic and adversarial search and constraint propagation, explaining admissibility, pruning and termination.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compiler Construction
decks.description: Translate source programs into executable code.

includes: Parsing, intermediate representations, dataflow optimization and code generation

practice: Build an end-to-end compiler and use differential and generated tests to validate optimization and target execution.

outcomes.description: Generate target code with instruction selection, calling conventions and register allocation; validate against interpreter behavior.
Implement lexical analysis, parsing, name resolution and type checking for a specified source grammar.
Construct control-flow and intermediate representations; implement fixed-point dataflow analyses and semantics-preserving local optimizations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation
decks.description: Establish computational possibility and resource limits.

includes: Automata, grammars, Turing computation, undecidability and NP-completeness

practice: Classify unfamiliar language and decision problems with constructions, reductions and carefully bounded impossibility claims.

outcomes.description: Define time and space classes, verify certificates and prove NP-completeness with polynomial reductions.
Construct Turing-machine models and prove undecidability through diagonalization and computable reductions.
Construct and transform finite automata, regular expressions, context-free grammars and pushdown machines; prove expressiveness limits.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures
decks.description: Implement and select efficient data organizations.

includes: Lists, trees, hashing, heaps, graphs, recursion and asymptotic costs

practice: Implement competing indexes for the same workload and defend correctness and measured versus predicted costs.

outcomes.description: Derive worst-case and amortized operation costs and choose structures from workload and memory requirements.
Use recursion and representation invariants to establish correctness and generate structural tests.
Implement linked structures, hash tables, search trees, heaps and adjacency representations with documented operations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Databases
decks.description: Design reliable storage and retrieval systems.

includes: Relational design, SQL, indexes, query plans, transactions and alternative data models

practice: Build a constrained database, optimize a workload and reproduce and repair an isolation anomaly.

outcomes.description: Translate requirements into schemas, keys and constraints; normalize relations and compare document and graph models.
Write relational-algebra and SQL queries and explain join, index and query-plan costs.
Analyze isolation anomalies, serializability, locking, logging and crash recovery using explicit transaction histories.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Digital Systems
decks.description: Construct computational hardware at the logic level.

includes: Binary arithmetic, Boolean circuits, state machines and synchronous logic

practice: Implement an arithmetic controller in a logic simulator and verify normal, overflow and reset behavior.

outcomes.description: Encode integers, floating-point values and characters; calculate overflow, rounding and bitwise operations.
Derive Boolean expressions and construct combinational arithmetic, multiplexing and decoding circuits.
Build clocked finite-state controllers from registers and combinational logic; test timing and state transitions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed Systems
decks.description: Build services that remain coherent under partial failure.

includes: Failure models, logical time, consistency, consensus, replication and distributed operation

practice: Implement a replicated service and validate histories during crashes, delay and partitions against an explicit consistency specification.

outcomes.description: Model asynchronous executions, clocks, failures and consistency; prove bounded safety and liveness claims and explain impossibility results.
Operate and fault-test distributed services using observability, backpressure, retries and idempotence with measured reliability tradeoffs.
Implement replicated logs and transactions and analyze consensus, quorum and recovery behavior under partitions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Methods
decks.description: Specify and verify computational behavior.

includes: Program logic, transition systems, temporal logic, model checking and proof-assisted verification

practice: Verify a small stateful protocol or program with both manual invariants and machine-checked obligations.

outcomes.description: Write preconditions, postconditions and loop invariants and prove partial and total correctness using Hoare-style rules.
Specify finite transition systems and temporal properties and implement bounded reachability and model-checking procedures.
Encode verification obligations in documented solver or proof-assistant tools and analyze counterexamples, abstraction and trusted assumptions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics
decks.description: Construct images from geometric scene representations.

includes: Three-dimensional transforms, geometric visibility, rasterization, ray tracing and image sampling

practice: Build a renderer and image-processing pipeline and verify visibility, projection and sampling behavior against constructed reference scenes.

outcomes.description: Construct homogeneous transformations, camera projections and ray-surface intersections for three-dimensional scenes.
Implement image convolution, resampling and curve interpolation; diagnose aliasing, color-space and geometric artifacts.
Implement triangle rasterization, depth testing and a basic ray tracer with explicitly taught local illumination models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction
decks.description: Design and evaluate usable, inclusive interfaces.

includes: User research, interaction prototypes, accessibility, usability studies and design ethics

practice: Prototype an accessible interface and redesign it from an approved or simulated usability study with documented tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Translate observed user needs into task models, interaction prototypes and accessibility requirements.
Design usability tests and controlled comparisons; analyze completion, error and qualitative evidence with sampling limitations.
Justify interface and data-collection choices against consent, manipulation, exclusion and competing stakeholder obligations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning
decks.description: Develop and evaluate data-driven predictive models.

includes: Supervised learning, unsupervised representations, neural-network basics and responsible evaluation

practice: Implement baseline learners and a neural model on unfamiliar data, comparing reproducible validation and subgroup error evidence.

outcomes.description: Construct leakage-free validation, calibration and error analyses; assess imbalance, subgroup harms, privacy and distribution shift.
Implement clustering, principal components and a small neural network with backpropagation; interpret representation and optimization choices.
Derive and implement linear and logistic regression, regularized losses, gradient training and basic decision-tree learning.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks
decks.description: Implement and diagnose network communication.

includes: Layering, addressing, routing, transport, sockets and packet diagnosis

practice: Implement a reliable file-transfer protocol in an impaired network emulator and explain packet-level failure evidence.

outcomes.description: Analyze packet captures and throughput-delay calculations to distinguish routing, loss, congestion and application failures.
Explain link framing, addressing, routing, naming and layered encapsulation with concrete packet representations.
Implement socket applications and bounded reliable-delivery protocols using sequence numbers, acknowledgments, timeouts and flow control.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems
decks.description: Implement and explain resource-sharing mechanisms.

includes: Processes, synchronization, memory management, filesystems and operating-system interfaces

practice: Extend an instructional kernel or emulator with synchronization and memory features and test adversarial execution schedules.

outcomes.description: Explain and implement bounded allocation and virtual-memory policies with protection and page-replacement analysis.
Implement process scheduling and synchronization; reason about races, deadlock, atomicity and concurrent invariants.
Implement filesystem and I/O exercises and analyze crash consistency, permissions and system-call behavior.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations
decks.description: Construct reliable small programs from specifications.

includes: Sequential programming, structured data, files, debugging and tests

practice: Build a file-processing application with malformed-input handling, automated tests and a reproducible execution guide.

outcomes.description: Process strings, lists, mappings and files; explain values, references, mutation and exceptions.
Write programs using variables, expressions, conditionals, loops, functions and explicit input-output contracts.
Trace execution, debug failures and construct boundary, property-based and regression tests.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages
decks.description: Explain and implement language meaning and abstraction.

includes: Operational semantics, interpreters, types, binding and programming paradigms

practice: Implement two evaluation strategies for a typed language and use proofs and tests to expose their behavioral differences.

outcomes.description: Compare functional, object-oriented and declarative abstraction through equivalent programs and modularity tradeoffs.
Define operational rules and implement interpreters with environments, closures, mutation and explicit evaluation strategies.
Construct a simple static type checker and prove bounded progress and preservation claims by structural induction.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Security and Privacy
decks.description: Evaluate and defend computing systems.

includes: Threat modeling, application and systems attacks, cryptographic use, privacy and defense
excludes: Unauthorized exploitation and advanced cryptographic proofs

practice: Threat-model an isolated application, demonstrate authorized vulnerabilities and verify fixes with regression and abuse-case tests.

outcomes.description: Explain modular arithmetic, encryption, authentication, signatures and key exchange; select standard primitives and diagnose protocol misuse.
Implement least privilege, validation and monitoring; justify privacy, disclosure and incident-response decisions with evidence.
Construct threat models and reproduce bounded memory, injection, authentication and network attacks in authorized sandboxes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Software Engineering
decks.description: Deliver maintainable software under real constraints.

includes: Requirements, modular design, testing, version control, delivery and professional tradeoffs

practice: Deliver a team-maintained application change through requirements negotiation, code review, continuous testing and a release retrospective.

outcomes.description: Use version control, issue tracking, automated builds and release procedures; diagnose regressions and document operational risks.
Design modular interfaces, refactor code and construct unit, integration and property-based tests with reviewable evidence.
Elicit and prioritize requirements, define acceptance criteria and justify privacy, accessibility and stakeholder tradeoffs.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Abstract Algebra
decks.description: Analyze mathematical structure through algebraic invariants.

includes: Groups, actions, quotient structures, rings, ideals, polynomials and fields
excludes: Galois theory and advanced representation theory

practice: Classify an unfamiliar small algebraic structure and prove its quotient and field-extension properties.

outcomes.description: Construct finite fields and elementary field extensions and determine minimal polynomials and extension degrees.
Prove group and homomorphism properties; calculate actions, quotient groups and finite-group structure using Sylow theorems.
Construct quotient rings and ideals; prove divisibility and factorization results in integers and polynomial rings.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology
decks.description: Distinguish spaces with algebraic invariants.

includes: Fundamental groups, coverings, chain complexes, homology and exact-sequence calculations

practice: Compute fundamental groups and homology of unfamiliar glued spaces and prove a topological obstruction.

outcomes.description: Prove bounded invariance, fixed-point and nonretraction consequences and compare spaces through computable invariants.
Construct simplicial and singular chain complexes and compute homology with boundary maps and exact sequences.
Calculate fundamental groups and covering-space relationships using homotopy and van Kampen arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus
decks.description: Calculate change, accumulation and approximation.

includes: Limits, derivatives, integrals, differential models and series in one variable

practice: Derive an accumulation model, calculate its optimum and compare exact, graphical and Taylor-based solutions.

outcomes.description: Calculate limits and derivatives and solve related-rate, extremum and local-linearization problems.
Apply the fundamental theorem, substitution, integration by parts and improper integrals to accumulation models.
Analyze sequences and series; construct Taylor approximations and bound truncation errors under stated conditions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Combinatorics and Graph Theory
decks.description: Count finite structures and prove graph properties.

includes: Enumerative methods, formal generating functions, graph invariants and extremal arguments

practice: Count constrained objects in two ways and prove a sharp or bounded graph-theoretic claim.

outcomes.description: Solve counting problems with bijections, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences and formal generating functions.
Establish elementary extremal and Ramsey bounds using double counting, induction and pigeonhole arguments.
Prove results about trees, connectivity, matchings, colorings and planar graphs using explicit constructions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Exploit analytic structure in complex-variable problems.

includes: Holomorphic functions, contour integration, residues, conformal maps and harmonic applications

practice: Evaluate a parameterized real integral by residues and solve a transformed planar boundary-value problem.

outcomes.description: Analyze complex differentiability, power series and analytic continuation; prove elementary Cauchy-Riemann and holomorphic-function results.
Use conformal maps and analytic functions to evaluate real integrals and solve bounded harmonic-potential problems.
Prove and apply Cauchy integral results, Laurent expansions and residue methods with explicit contour estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations and Dynamics
decks.description: Model and analyze finite-dimensional evolution.

includes: First-order equations, linear higher-order equations, systems, phase portraits and elementary numerical stepping

practice: Derive a coupled flow model, solve its linear case and compare phase portraits and time-step approximations.

outcomes.description: Construct phase portraits, linearize equilibria, classify stability and implement hand-calculated Euler steps with error comparisons.
Solve separable and linear first-order equations and constant-coefficient forced second-order initial-value problems.
Solve linear systems using eigenstructure and matrix exponentials; interpret coupled state representations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
decks.description: Calculate intrinsic and extrinsic geometry.

includes: Parametrized curves and surfaces, curvature, fundamental forms and geodesics

practice: Compare intrinsic and extrinsic geometry on unfamiliar surfaces and calculate geodesics in selected coordinate charts.

outcomes.description: Calculate arc length, curvature, torsion and moving frames of curves in two and three dimensions.
Derive surface geodesic equations and compare intrinsic distances, parallel transport and local curvature effects.
Compute tangent planes, first and second fundamental forms, Gaussian and mean curvature of parametrized surfaces.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantitative and Spatial Foundations
decks.description: Represent and solve elementary quantitative problems.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, units, elementary geometry, trigonometry and coordinate vectors

practice: Model an unfamiliar geometric measurement problem, solve it algebraically and check units, scale and graphical consistency.

outcomes.description: Manipulate fractions, powers, logarithms, equations and inequalities; interpret polynomial, exponential and trigonometric functions.
Calculate lengths, areas, volumes and angles; use similarity, trigonometry and two- or three-dimensional coordinate vectors.
Translate tables, graphs and verbal models into equations; track units, scales, significant figures and estimation errors.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis
decks.description: Analyze infinite-dimensional linear and variational problems.

includes: Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality, bounded operators, weak convergence and spectral theory

practice: Establish existence and spectral approximation for an unfamiliar compact-operator or coercive variational problem.

outcomes.description: Apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping results; analyze weak convergence and operator adjoints.
Construct Banach, Hilbert and Lp spaces and prove completeness, projection and duality results.
Prove compact self-adjoint spectral results and solve bounded variational and eigenfunction approximation problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra
decks.description: Use structural algebraic methods at graduate depth.

includes: Modules, structure theorems, Galois theory and finite-group representations

practice: Determine a splitting field and Galois group and decompose a related finite-dimensional group representation.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply Galois correspondence and determine solvability and constructibility for polynomial examples.
Construct modules, tensor products and exact sequences and apply structure theorems over principal ideal domains.
Construct finite-group representations and character tables and prove decomposition and orthogonality results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Analysis and PDE
decks.description: Establish and approximate weak field solutions.

includes: Distributions, Sobolev spaces, weak formulations, energy methods and Galerkin approximation

practice: Prove well-posedness for a weak boundary problem and implement a mesh-refinement study verifying its approximation estimate.

outcomes.description: Derive and implement Galerkin and elementary finite-element approximations and establish bounded convergence and error estimates.
Prove bounded elliptic and evolutionary existence, uniqueness and stability results using coercivity, compactness and energy estimates.
Construct distributions and Sobolev spaces and formulate weak derivatives, traces and boundary-value problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra
decks.description: Represent and solve finite-dimensional linear problems.

includes: Linear systems, vector spaces, linear maps, eigenproblems and least squares

practice: Recover a linear transformation from data and compare exact inversion with least-squares and singular-value solutions.

outcomes.description: Construct bases and coordinate changes; prove elementary claims about vector spaces and linear maps.
Compute eigenstructure, orthogonal projections, least-squares solutions, quadratic forms and singular-value decompositions.
Solve matrix systems by elimination; characterize rank, null spaces, consistency and determinants.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Logic
decks.description: Analyze formal mathematical theories and their limits.

includes: First-order proof systems, completeness, compactness, models and incompleteness

practice: Formalize a theory, construct a compactness application and present a complete bounded incompleteness argument.

outcomes.description: Formalize first-order syntax, semantics and derivations and prove soundness and bounded completeness constructions.
Develop arithmetization and representability sufficiently to prove a stated incompleteness theorem and distinguish its assumptions.
Apply compactness and elementary model constructions to distinguish semantic consequence, categoricity and expressibility.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Manifolds and Riemannian Geometry
decks.description: Construct coordinate-independent smooth geometry.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tangent bundles, tensors, differential forms, connections and curvature

practice: Describe a manifold in overlapping charts and compute invariant integrals, geodesics and curvature independently in both.

outcomes.description: Compute metrics, Levi-Civita connections, geodesics and curvature tensors and distinguish intrinsic geometric invariants.
Calculate differential forms, exterior derivatives and pullbacks and prove and apply manifold Stokes theorem in bounded settings.
Construct smooth atlases, tangent and cotangent bundles, vector fields and tensor transformations on explicit manifolds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Statistics
decks.description: Derive statistical procedures from probability models.

includes: Joint densities, transformations, likelihood, Bayesian inference and linear statistical models

practice: Derive and compare exact, asymptotic and Bayesian intervals for a new parametric sampling model.

outcomes.description: Calculate joint, marginal and transformed densities, moments and sampling distributions using multivariable integration.
Derive moment, likelihood and conjugate Bayesian estimators; compare bias, variance, sufficiency and information bounds.
Derive likelihood-ratio tests and linear-model inference; apply stated central-limit and large-sample approximations with diagnostics.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure and Integration
decks.description: Establish rigorous integration and convergence tools.

includes: Sigma-algebras, measure construction, Lebesgue integration, product measures and convergence theorems

practice: Construct convergence counterexamples and prove an unfamiliar parameter-dependent integration result.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply monotone and dominated convergence and distinguish almost-everywhere, measure and norm convergence.
Construct the Lebesgue integral and product measures; apply Fubini, Tonelli and Radon-Nikodym results with hypotheses.
Construct measures from outer measures and analyze measurable sets, functions and null-set distinctions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
decks.description: Calculate with functions and fields in several dimensions.

includes: Partial derivatives, multiple integrals, coordinate changes and vector integral theorems

practice: Compute mass, flux and a constrained optimum for a three-dimensional model, checking coordinate-independent agreement.

outcomes.description: Compute gradients, Jacobians and Hessians; apply chain rules, local approximations and Lagrange multipliers.
Calculate line and surface integrals, divergence and curl; apply Green, Stokes and divergence theorems.
Evaluate multiple integrals in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates with correct Jacobians.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Number Theory
decks.description: Prove arithmetic structure and solve integer constraints.

includes: Divisibility, congruences, quadratic residues and elementary Diophantine methods
excludes: Arithmetic geometry and analytic number theory

practice: Solve an unfamiliar integer equation and prove the completeness or explicit limits of the solution method.

outcomes.description: Prove divisibility and prime-factorization results and apply Euclidean and arithmetic-function methods.
Solve modular systems and establish Fermat, Euler and elementary quadratic-reciprocity consequences.
Solve bounded Diophantine problems using descent, congruences, continued fractions and rational approximation.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Methods
decks.description: Implement and validate numerical calculations.

includes: Floating-point error, conditioning, numerical linear algebra, interpolation, quadrature and ODE integration

practice: Build a tested numerical library and expose failure cases involving ill-conditioning, unstable steps and misleading residuals.

outcomes.description: Implement root finding, pivoted linear solves, least squares, interpolation and quadrature; compare convergence and cost.
Implement Euler and Runge-Kutta integration from locally defined initial-value models; assess stability and step-size convergence.
Distinguish conditioning, stability, truncation and roundoff; calculate error bounds and residual-based diagnostics.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization
decks.description: Formulate and solve finite-dimensional optimization problems.

includes: Linear and convex models, constrained optimality, duality and numerical optimization

practice: Solve a constrained allocation and fitting problem, checking optimality certificates and sensitivity to initialization and scaling.

outcomes.description: Implement gradient, Newton and projected methods; explain line search and compare with documented linear-programming solvers.
Translate constraints and objectives into linear, quadratic or convex programs and diagnose infeasibility and scaling.
Derive first- and second-order conditions, KKT systems and elementary dual bounds under stated regularity assumptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations
decks.description: Solve classical field evolution and boundary problems.

includes: Linear PDE classification, characteristics, separation, Fourier methods and Green functions

practice: Solve the same forced heat problem by eigenfunction expansion and Green-function convolution, checking boundaries and limiting behavior.

outcomes.description: Formulate initial and boundary data and classify transport, heat, wave and elliptic equations; solve elementary characteristics.
Solve rectangular and radially symmetric boundary problems by separation, eigenfunction expansions and Fourier coefficients.
Use explicitly developed Fourier transforms and Green functions to solve linear source problems and check conservation and uniqueness.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability Foundations
decks.description: Build elementary models of uncertainty.

includes: Counting, conditional probability, random variables and standard distributions without calculus prerequisites
excludes: Measure theory and proofs of continuous limit theorems

practice: Compare competing probability models for an unfamiliar observation process using exact enumeration and supplied distribution tables.

outcomes.description: Interpret continuous densities as areas; use normal and exponential distribution functions and explain sampling variability.
Construct sample spaces, count combinations and calculate conditional probabilities, independence and Bayesian updates.
Calculate discrete expectations, variances, joint distributions and binomial or Poisson predictions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis
decks.description: Justify the foundations and limits of calculus.

includes: Real completeness, metric limits, continuity, compactness and function-sequence convergence

practice: Develop proofs and counterexamples for a family of parameterized function sequences and their integral limits.

outcomes.description: Prove continuity, compactness, differentiation and Riemann-integration results with explicit hypotheses and counterexamples.
Distinguish pointwise and uniform convergence and justify exchanging limits, derivatives and integrals in bounded settings.
Prove sequence and series convergence using completeness, Cauchy criteria and rigorous estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Reasoning
decks.description: Construct precise elementary mathematical arguments.

includes: Logic, proof, sets, functions, elementary counting and Euclidean constructions

practice: Write and revise proofs of a counting identity, a divisibility claim and an unfamiliar geometric construction.

outcomes.description: Prove elementary congruence and similarity claims and justify straightedge-and-compass constructions from stated axioms.
Use quantifiers, direct proof, contradiction and induction; diagnose invalid arguments and construct counterexamples.
Work with sets, relations, functions, bijections, finite counting and countable sets.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Statistical Inference
decks.description: Establish graduate statistical guarantees.

includes: Asymptotic estimation, decision theory, Bayesian consistency and nonparametric foundations

practice: Prove an estimator's asymptotic behavior and test coverage and decision risk in an unfamiliar nonparametric setting.

outcomes.description: Develop convergence-in-distribution tools and prove bounded consistency, central-limit and delta-method results for estimators.
Compare estimators through risk, admissibility, minimax and Bayesian criteria and establish bounded posterior-consistency results.
Derive kernel, resampling and regularized nonparametric procedures and analyze bias-variance and confidence-coverage limitations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Reasoning
decks.description: Make defensible introductory inferences from data.

includes: Sampling, estimation, hypothesis tests, resampling and simple regression using documented software

practice: Analyze a new observational and randomized dataset in documented software, reporting diagnostics and competing interpretations.

outcomes.description: Design sampling and randomized comparisons; identify confounding, selection bias, dependence and misleading summaries.
Calculate and interpret confidence intervals, tests and bootstrap estimates; check assumptions and distinguish statistical from practical significance.
Fit and diagnose simple linear regression, compare predictions and explain limits on causal interpretation.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability and Stochastic Processes
decks.description: Analyze random evolution and its approximations.

includes: Measure-theoretic probability, Markov chains, martingales, Brownian motion and elementary stochastic calculus

practice: Prove a stopping or convergence result and compare analytic hitting predictions with a validated stochastic simulation.

outcomes.description: Construct probability spaces and conditional expectations and prove bounded laws of large numbers and convergence results.
Analyze Markov chains, Poisson processes, stopping times and martingales; calculate stationary and hitting behavior.
Construct Brownian and L2 Ito integrals, apply Ito formula and solve and simulate elementary stochastic differential equations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Point-Set Topology
decks.description: Reason about spaces independently of coordinates.

includes: Topological spaces, continuity, compactness, connectedness and product and quotient constructions

practice: Classify unfamiliar quotient-space examples and prove or refute compactness and connectedness claims.

outcomes.description: Prove compactness and connectedness results and construct counterexamples distinguishing related notions.
Analyze product and quotient spaces and establish homeomorphisms or topological obstructions in concrete examples.
Construct topologies and continuous maps and compare metric, subspace, separation and countability properties.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Analyze realistic quantum systems beyond exact solutions.

includes: Approximation theory, transitions, scattering, identical particles, density matrices and open systems

practice: Compare approximation methods for an unfamiliar transition or scattering problem and model a reduced-state decoherence experiment.

outcomes.description: Derive stationary and time-dependent perturbation, variational and semiclassical approximations and calculate transition rates.
Construct identical-particle and composite states, reduced density matrices and bounded master equations; quantify entanglement and decoherence.
Calculate three-dimensional scattering with partial waves, Born approximation and Green functions; check unitarity and cross sections.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics
decks.description: Derive mechanics from variational and phase-space principles.

includes: Variational mechanics, generalized coordinates, Hamiltonian structure and nonlinear dynamics

practice: Derive and analyze a constrained coupled mechanical system in both Lagrangian and Hamiltonian representations.

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, canonical equations, Poisson brackets and elementary canonical transformations.
Analyze normal modes, phase-space stability, separatrices and bounded examples of nonlinear resonance and chaos.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations, constrained-coordinate models and Noether conservation laws through explicit action variations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astrophysics
decks.description: Infer cosmic systems from remote observations.

includes: Astronomical coordinates, photometry, spectra, stellar structure, galactic dynamics and elementary cosmology

practice: Analyze calibrated astronomical images and spectra to estimate stellar or galactic properties and compare competing physical interpretations.

outcomes.description: Infer galactic masses and compare expansion, dark-matter and cosmic-background evidence using explicitly supplied Friedmann-model relations.
Use celestial coordinates, distances, fluxes, magnitudes and Doppler spectra; calibrate images and infer properties with selection effects.
Construct hydrostatic, energy-generation and radiative-transport stellar models and interpret stellar evolution and compact-object evidence.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Computational Physics
decks.description: Implement and validate predictive physical models.

includes: Particle simulation, finite-difference fields, numerical validation and inverse physical modeling

practice: Build a forward field solver and recover source parameters from noisy synthetic observations with an identifiability audit.

outcomes.description: Implement finite-difference heat, wave and Poisson solvers; derive bounded stability conditions and test grid convergence.
Estimate hidden model parameters with weighted fitting and regularization; analyze sensitivity, nonuniqueness and predictive uncertainty.
Implement particle and oscillator simulations with conservation-aware integration and convergence comparisons.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed Matter Physics
decks.description: Predict collective and electronic properties of solids.

includes: Crystals, diffraction, phonons, bands, semiconductors, transport and ordered phases

practice: Infer a solid's lattice and carrier behavior from diffraction, heat-capacity and transport data using competing models.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary Bloch and tight-binding bands and calculate carrier populations, semiconductor junctions and transport coefficients.
Construct reciprocal lattices and calculate diffraction, lattice vibrations and phonon contributions to thermodynamic behavior.
Analyze magnetic, superconducting and structural phases using order parameters, symmetry and bounded phenomenological models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electricity and Circuits
decks.description: Calculate and test elementary electrical systems.

includes: Point-charge electrostatics, potential, resistive networks, capacitors and circuit measurement
excludes: Maxwell field theory and AC differential equations

practice: Design a sensor-divider circuit and reconcile measured voltages with loading, tolerance and uncertainty predictions.

outcomes.description: Solve resistive networks with Ohm and Kirchhoff laws; calculate power, equivalent circuits and steady-state capacitance.
Build and diagnose low-voltage circuits, accounting for meter loading, tolerances and safe power limits.
Calculate point-charge forces, fields, potentials and capacitor energy using vector superposition and bounded geometries.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electromagnetism
decks.description: Solve classical electromagnetic field problems.

includes: Field boundary problems, magnetism, induction, Maxwell equations, waves and radiation

practice: Solve a dielectric boundary and antenna problem, checking Maxwell boundary conditions and energy accounting.

outcomes.description: Apply Maxwell equations, induction and constitutive models; solve AC circuits and plane-wave interface problems.
Calculate electromagnetic energy, momentum and bounded dipole-radiation patterns using retarded potentials.
Solve electrostatic and magnetostatic problems using potentials, symmetry, multipoles, images and material boundary conditions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics
decks.description: Construct instrumented tests of physical models.

includes: Electronic instrumentation, sampling, spectral analysis, calibrated experiments and model discrimination

practice: Build an instrumented resonance or optical experiment and submit code, calibration records, spectral diagnostics and a model-comparison report.

outcomes.description: Fit physical models with weighted residuals and uncertainty budgets; design experiments distinguishing model failure from systematic error.
Construct sensor and amplifier chains using taught op-amp models, filters, grounding and calibrated acquisition procedures.
Implement discrete Fourier analysis and analyze sampling, aliasing, bandwidth, noise spectra and lock-in detection.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluid and Continuum Mechanics
decks.description: Model flowing continua and identify governing regimes.

includes: Continuum stress, conservation, viscous flow, dimensional analysis, waves and compressibility

practice: Derive and test a flow model for unfamiliar geometry, comparing exact profiles, scaling estimates and measured pressure loss.

outcomes.description: Derive continuity, momentum and energy balances using control volumes, stress tensors and constitutive assumptions.
Solve hydrostatic, potential, channel and creeping flows and apply boundary-layer scaling and drag estimates.
Use dimensionless groups to analyze stability, surface waves, compressible flow and shock jump conditions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity
decks.description: Predict gravity through spacetime geometry.

includes: Lorentzian geometry, Einstein equations, black holes, gravitational waves and relativistic cosmology

practice: Compute observables in an unfamiliar symmetric metric and compare a cosmological solution with supplied distance data.
